descriptionChirho: The open hand or palm, used of persons grasping, holding, striking, or as a surface for placing objects; Arabic kaff confirms the primary Semitic meaning.
The bottom surface of the foot; distinguished from palm by Arabic bāṭin/asfal/akhmaṣ (not kaff) and Korean 발바닥 (balbadak) rather than 손바닥 (sonbadak).
The padded underside of an animal's foot, a zoological extension of the palm/sole meaning; Korean 발바닥 with animal possessive suffix and Hindi पंजा (panja) confirm the animal sense.
The hollow of the thigh joint or hip socket, as in Jacob's wrestling; Arabic ḥuqq (socket/hollow) clearly distinguishes this from the flat-surface senses.
A palm-shaped cultic vessel used for incense or offerings in the tabernacle and temple; Arabic ku'ūs (cups) or ṣuḥūn (dishes) and Korean 숟가락/접시 confirm the utensil meaning.
The handle or grip of a door bolt or lock, shaped like a palm; Arabic kaffūt and Korean 손잡이 (sonjabi, handle) distinguish it from body-part senses.
A branch or frond of a palm tree, from the resemblance of the leaf spread to an open hand; Arabic sa'af (palm frond) uniquely identifies this botanical sense.
